<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-preset-comparands.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts`, `packages/verify/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via this_month (literal, a string literal in DATE_RANGE_PRESETS))_
- `content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx`  _(via DATE_RANGE_PRESETS (symbol, a top-level const object), last_month (literal, a string literal in DATE_RANGE_PRESETS), last_quarter (literal, a string literal in DATE_RANGE_PRESETS), next_30_days (literal, a string literal in DATE_RANGE_PRESETS), next_month (literal, a string literal in DATE_RANGE_PRESETS), next_quarter (literal, a string literal in DATE_RANGE_PRESETS), this_month (literal, a string literal in DATE_RANGE_PRESETS), this_quarter (literal, a string literal in DATE_RANGE_PRESETS))_
- `content/docs/ui/reports.mdx`  _(via this_month (literal, a string literal in DATE_RANGE_PRESETS), this_quarter (literal, a string literal in DATE_RANGE_PRESETS))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-preset-comparands.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts`, `packages/verify/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **179** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a9fb14bdeeb5e09fec341ead4e0fffd8d8ed00bb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3222cacf7151968084b89450032a330adf838b53` — the merge of head `5af3917a89fc44c756aef0dfb386824b19e323f3` into base `a9fb14bdeeb5e09fec341ead4e0fffd8d8ed00bb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3222cacf7151968084b89450032a330adf838b53 && git checkout 3222cacf7151968084b89450032a330adf838b53
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a9fb14bdeeb5e09fec341ead4e0fffd8d8ed00bb 5af3917a89fc44c756aef0dfb386824b19e323f3 && git checkout -B drift-repro a9fb14bdeeb5e09fec341ead4e0fffd8d8ed00bb && git merge --no-ff 5af3917a89fc44c756aef0dfb386824b19e323f3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a9fb14bdeeb5e09fec341ead4e0fffd8d8ed00bb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a9fb14bdeeb5e09fec341ead4e0fffd8d8ed00bb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f7e8b2034a08adcb10e71b6f7f1d08873dd91ac4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: the full diff (28 files) against merge-base f68b47ca; card #30076 and its 5 comments; PR #30133 body and 2 issue comments (0 review comments); check-runs on the head; packages/spec/src/data/date-range-presets.ts, date-range-presets.test.ts, date-macros.zod.ts:108-266, ui/dashboard.zod.ts:1474, ui/report.zod.ts:704, data/analytics.zod.ts:739-842; packages/core/src/utils/analytics-date-range.ts, analytics-date-range.test.ts (NOW, SWEEP, #17341 and #30076 blocks), analytics-date-range-conformance.ts, filter-tokens.ts:269-520, datetime.ts:100-160; packages/lint/src/validate-preset-comparands.ts; packages/objectql/src/temporal-comparand-door.ts; packages/verify/src/dashboard-window.ts:86-766, packages/verify/README.md:40-170; ui/packages/core/src/utils/date-macros.ts, dashboard-filters.ts, compare-to.ts:55-140, __tests__/dashboard-filters.presetWindows-29116.test.ts; ui/packages/components/src/custom/filter-builder.tsx, filterRelativeDates.ts, __tests__/filter-builder-relative-dates-29115.test.tsx; ui/packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DashboardFilterBar.tsx, DatasetWidget.tsx:244-275, README.md:415; ui/packages/plugin-report/src/ReportDateRange.tsx; ui/packages/types/src/data-protocol.ts:590-610; the 10 locale packs; content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx, content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx:2590-2606, content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx:140-185; .changeset/30076-forward-date-range-presets.md and .changeset/config.json; #29349 ruling F (comment 6580070604 and the 四棱(F) text).

### ① Derived judgments

1. Extents hold. Spec rows (date-range-presets.ts:154-156) are inclusive: `next_month` = `[{next_month_start},{next_month_end}]`, `next_quarter` = `[{next_quarter_start},{next_quarter_end}]`, `next_30_days` = `[{today},{30_days_from_now}]`, i.e. today through the 30th day ahead = 31 calendar days, the exact mirror of `last_30_days` (31 days, `[{30_days_ago},{today}]`); both pinned at 31 by `prescribedDayCount` (date-range-presets.test.ts:464,467) and the three rows are in `EXPECTED_WINDOW_DAYS` (:179-181) and `TOKEN_DAY_ON_REFERENCE` (:146-150). Core's half-open form (analytics-date-range.ts:168-170) covers the same days: `next_30_days` stops before `31_days_from_now` (Sep 9 → Oct 10 excl. = 31 days, test :246); `next_month`/`next_quarter` stop at `next_*_start` re-anchored on the day `next_*_start` names (:329,:368-372). The #17341 sweep (test :396-409) iterates every `DATE_RANGE_PRESETS` member over 8 instants × 4 zones, including 2026-12-31T23:59Z and 2026-01-01 (December and Q4 rollovers), and holds each core end to `nextUtcCalendarDay(resolveFilterToken(specEnd))` in the same zone, so the two conventions are tied by the one resolver, not by hand. Concrete rows pin UTC year-cross (:245), Shanghai day-already-February (:249), New York DST end/start (:252-254) and Chatham +13:45/+12:45 (:256). The core conformance kit iterates `DATE_RANGE_PRESETS` (analytics-date-range-conformance.ts:184), so service-analytics and driver-memory are judged on the three without edits.
2. Re-anchoring zone: `boundDayStart` passes the same `timezone` to both `tokenDayStartMs(from)` and `tokenDayStart(token, anchor)` (analytics-date-range.ts:368-372); `resolveFilterToken` derives today via `proxyDay(now, timezone)` (filter-tokens.ts:269,414) and all arithmetic is UTC-proxy; no local-clock call anywhere. One hazard (should-fix, ② below): the anchor round-trips through an INSTANT, local midnight of the `from` day (`zonedDateStartToUtcMs`), and datetime.ts:146-150 documents that a wall clock the zone skips settles on the post-transition offset, "just before the gap", which reads as 23:xx of the PREVIOUS day locally. A zone whose spring-forward is 00:00 on the first day of a month or quarter then re-anchors on the last day of the prior period, `next_month_start` seen from there IS the anchor day, and the window is `[start, start)`, empty. tz-db case: America/Asuncion, 2023-10-01 00:00 → 01:00 (first Sunday of October rule; Oct 1 2023 was a Sunday), so `next_month` from 2023-09-15 and `next_quarter` from 2023-07-15 in that zone resolve empty. No current zone has such a rule for future dates, and the sweep zones do not include one, so it is latent; the existing 13 presets render each bound once and never round-trip. Fix: re-anchor on the day's noon (`zonedWallClockToUtcMs({…day, hour: 12}, tz)`), as ui date-macros.ts:63 already does for the same reason, and add an Asuncion-2023 row.
3. Readers. Every vocabulary reader on the head derives from the spec: spec analytics.zod.ts:739 (`z.enum(DATE_RANGE_PRESETS)`), dashboard.zod.ts:1474, report.zod.ts:704, filter.zod.ts, lint validate-preset-comparands.ts, core resolver/conformance, verify dashboard-window.ts:761, ui dashboard-filters.ts:25-26, filterRelativeDates.ts:92-100, filter-builder.tsx, DashboardFilterBar.tsx:285, ReportDateRange.tsx:218. No source reader holds a stale list or count. Stale prose remains in three hand-written places the PR did not touch: packages/verify/README.md:44 ("each of the 13 presets") and :167 ("never after today", now false since dashboard-window.ts:607-610 writes a forward window's future edges); content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx:2594 ("never after today") and :2600 ("each of the 13 presets"), a page the docs-drift check named; ui/packages/plugin-dashboard/README.md:415 ("today | this_week | … | last_90_days | custom", the list no longer ends at `last_90_days`). validate-preset-comparands.ts:72 "13 declared preset names" is inside a verbatim quote of the 2026-09-06 ruling and is rightly left. The objectql door (temporal-comparand-door.ts) imports only `classifyFilterToken`/`isTextFilterOperator` and reads no vocabulary; it refuses any string on a temporal field, so it is unaffected, but the PR body's claim that it "iterates `DATE_RANGE_PRESETS`" is wrong (⑤).
4. UI edits are confined to readers that red: the three labels in all 10 packs (ar de en es fr ja ko pt ru zh; zh-Hant has no console pack yet, #29428 phase 2, so the same-PR follow at i18n-standard.mdx:160-162 is met for every language the surface carries); the English defaults table in filter-builder.tsx:1217-1226 (the 29115 test renders raw keys without it); `next_month_end`/`next_quarter_end` in date-macros.ts:132,134, correct (`endOfMonth(addMonths(startOfMonth(today),1))`, `endOfQuarter(addMonths(startOfQuarter(today),3))`), pinned across the year rollover and a leap February (29116 test :119-127); and the two count/order pins. Labels are correct native wording and match each pack's existing register: zh 下月/下季度/未来 30 天 (the ruling's own words), ja 来月/来四半期/今後 30 日間, ko 다음 달/다음 분기/향후 30일, de Nächster Monat/Nächstes Quartal/Nächste 30 Tage, fr Le mois prochain/Le trimestre prochain/30 prochains jours, es El próximo mes/El próximo trimestre/Próximos 30 días, pt Próximo mês/Próximo trimestre/Próximos 30 dias, ru Следующий месяц/Следующий квартал/Следующие 30 дней, ar الشهر القادم/الربع القادم/الـ 30 يومًا القادمة. `ui/packages/types/src/data-protocol.ts:595-610` is a hand union that already lists the three (plus undeclared `next_year`, `next_7_days`, `next_90_days`); handed back as an observation, correctly not edited.
5. Inline compareTo (should-fix, filed not fixed): `shiftFilterByCompareTo(previousPeriod)` substitutes only `current_*`/`today` tokens (compare-to.ts:55-72), so a `next_month` window `[{next_month_start},{next_month_end}]` is its own "previous period" (delta 0), and `compareToTrendLabelKey` matches `/month_start/` and labels it "vs last month" (compare-to.ts:131-134). The dataset path (DatasetWidget.tsx:247-256) shifts the resolved window server-side and is right. The 29116 test narrowed its compareTo case from every preset to `RETIRED_PRESETS` (:151) without pinning what a forward preset does there or filing it; the PR body's "No `domain:ui` follow-up is needed" is stated for the preset list only and is true of that, but this inline-KPI reader needs a `domain:ui` card and a line in the body.
6. Verify: `fixtureDays` (dashboard-window.ts:602-614) adds the future edges only when `end > today`; the 13 existing presets' days are unchanged by construction (their ends are ≤ today). Windows are resolved on the caller's timezone (:756-764) and the family already declines a non-UTC caller (:1018), so the future-edge rows are UTC days like the rest.

### ② Semver level

Clause-② yes (widening): three new accepted values on `DATE_RANGE_PRESETS`, reaching `dashboard.dateRange.defaultRange`, the date global filter's `defaultValue`, `report.defaultRange` (report.zod.ts:704, via `DATE_RANGE_DEFAULT_RANGES`) and `AnalyticsQuery.timeDimensions[].dateRange` (analytics.zod.ts:739). Metadata-protocol: added is right: new values on authorable enums, no removal, no tightening. The changeset's seven levels cover every moved package: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/core` minor (new behaviour in the resolver), `@objectstack/lint` patch and `@objectstack/verify` patch (lint is prose only; verify changes fixture days, no API), `@object-ui/core` minor (two new client tokens), `@object-ui/components` minor, `@object-ui/i18n` minor. plugin-dashboard and plugin-report derive and are untouched. Nothing is narrowed: `PRESET_WINDOW_TOKENS` and `PresetWindowBound` are module-private (analytics-date-range.ts:329-334), the spec table's row type is unchanged, and the 13 existing rows are byte-identical. Check Changeset is green; `check-changeset-no-major` passed per the dev report.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs at read time: 23 completed (all success or skipped, incl. Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates, ESLint, PR-body guards) and 20 still in_progress (Test Core 1-8, Build Core/Docs/UI Deps, the Lint lanes, Type Check workspace/consumer/debt, Live E2E UI). No failure yet; the verdict below is on the code, and the seat must re-read the runs before merge.
- The PR body says `pnpm check:platform-checklist` exits 1 on a main-borne finding (platform-core.json anchor `assertProtocolCompat`); not this PR's, and the api-backend.json item moved to revision 3 / expect 16 correctly.
- Out-of-scope findings in the dev report (missing client `next_week_end`/`next_year_end`; the hand union in ui types) are correctly left out of this PR.
- The verify family proves forward windows only when the seed door accepts future-dated rows; the dev measured 15/15 green, and the api-backend.json knownGaps line now says a forward window needs future rows.

### ④ Design judgment

Re-anchoring is the right shape for the ruling: it names the month and quarter after next without a new macro token (`PERIOD_RE` stops at `next_`, filter-tokens.ts:371) and without calendar arithmetic in core, and the property test (test :264-277, "the end of next_X is the start of next_X as seen from inside next X") states exactly the invariant it relies on. Placing each forward preset after the backward member of its family keeps the 13 existing positions and reads as the ruling's three additions, not option B. The remaining defects are a latent DST-gap round trip in the re-anchor, stale prose in two READMEs and one docs page, a body claim about the objectql door, and an inline-compareTo reader that the test quietly stopped covering. None contradicts the ruling or the spec extents, so the verdict is PASS with should-fixes.

Should-fix 1: analytics-date-range.ts:368-372 re-anchors on local midnight; on a zone that skips 00:00 of a period's first day (America/Asuncion 2023-10-01) `next_month`/`next_quarter` resolve empty. Anchor on the day's noon and add that row.
Should-fix 2: update packages/verify/README.md:44,167, content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx:2594,2600 and ui/packages/plugin-dashboard/README.md:415 (13 presets; "never after today"; list ending at last_90_days).
Should-fix 3: PR body "objectql temporal-comparand-door.ts … iterate DATE_RANGE_PRESETS" is false; the door reads no vocabulary. Say it is unaffected because it is field-typed.
Should-fix 4: file a `domain:ui` card for compare-to.ts `previousPeriod` on forward windows (self-comparison, "vs last month" label) and name it in the PR body; restore or replace the compareTo coverage the 29116 test dropped for the three presets.

## Contract review — delta (fix round 1)

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `186fb6019ead8de9ede5fae9d73611f4e8d32bac`
Local-runs: none
Scope: the delta `git diff f7e8b203..186fb601` (6 files, one commit, merge-base still f68b47ca); record 6634808446 in full; the proposed body /mnt/project-files/seat3-orders/30076-body-r1.md against the live PR body; packages/core/src/utils/analytics-date-range.ts:120-240 (PresetWindowBound, PRESET_WINDOW_TOKENS, tokenDayStartMs, HALF_DAY_MS, boundDayStart, resolveAnalyticsDateRangePreset), analytics-date-range.test.ts:225-290 (#30076 block), datetime.ts:95-175 (zonedDateStartToUtcMs, zonedWallClockToUtcMs gap/overlap rules), filter-tokens.ts:269,417,450 (proxyDay); packages/verify/README.md:40-44,165-169; content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx:2586-2600; ui/packages/plugin-dashboard/README.md:415; ui/packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/dashboard-filters.presetWindows-29116.test.ts:60-75,140-170; compare-to.ts (diff stat: untouched); .changeset/30076-forward-date-range-presets.md (unchanged); cards #30134 and #30140; check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Should-fix 1 (noon anchor): closed. analytics-date-range.ts:200-201 defines `HALF_DAY_MS` and :218 anchors at `tokenDayStartMs(bound.from) + HALF_DAY_MS` before the second `resolveFilterToken` pass; :205-213 states the hazard and why noon. Only the re-anchored ends (`next_month`, `next_quarter`, :169-170) take this path; every string bound, i.e. both bounds of the 13 existing presets and of `next_30_days`, still goes through `tokenDayStart` unchanged (:217), so no existing window moves.
2. Can +12h leave the day? No, at both edges. The base the zone helper returns is local 00:00 on a normal day; +12h is 12:00 local (13:00 across a morning spring-forward, 11:00 across a morning fall-back), inside a 23-, 24- or 25-hour day. On the degenerate gap day the base is not the day's first instant but one gap-width BEFORE it (datetime.ts:146-150: a skipped wall clock settles just before the gap), so +12h lands 12h minus the gap into the day: for Asuncion 2023-10-01 that is 11h into a 23-hour day; even a 2-hour gap gives 10h into a 22-hour day. A fall-back at midnight makes 00:00 ambiguous and the helper takes the first occurrence (:151-153), which IS the day's first instant, and the day is 25h. Then `proxyDay` (filter-tokens.ts:269,417) reads the anchor's calendar parts in the same zone, so the second pass sees the anchor day as today. The one-line comment at :200 ("from a day's first instant") is slightly loose on the gap day, but :207-210 says the base reads as the day before, so the pair is correct together.
3. The two Asuncion rows (test :247-248) are right. Paraguay 2023: -04 standard, DST -03 from the first Sunday of October (2023-10-01) at 00:00 local to the fourth Sunday of March 2024. So 2023-10-01 00:00 -04 = 04:00Z is skipped straight to 01:00 -03. `next_month` from 2023-09-15T12:00Z (08:00 -04, Sep 15): `next_month_start` = 2023-10-01; helper → 00:00 at the post-gap offset -03 = 03:00Z (reads 23:00 -04 Sep 30); +12h = 15:00Z = 12:00 -03 Oct 1; `next_month_start` seen from Oct 1 = 2023-11-01, rendered at 00:00 -03 = 2023-11-01T03:00Z. `next_quarter` from 2023-08-15T12:00Z: anchor the same 15:00Z, `next_quarter_start` from Oct 1 = 2024-01-01, still DST, 00:00 -03 = 2024-01-01T03:00Z. Both rows match. Before the fix, the anchor 03:00Z read as Sep 30, `next_month_start` from there was Oct 1 again, `end === start`, as the record predicted.
4. The window's start instant 2023-10-01T03:00Z (23:00 -04 on Sep 30) is pre-existing zone-helper behaviour, not this PR's. It is `zonedDateStartToUtcMs('2023-10-01', 'America/Asuncion')` resolving a skipped midnight to the earlier candidate, documented and pinned in datetime.ts:140-150 and shared by every preset whose bound falls on that day (`this_month` or `this_quarter` on 2023-10-15 in Asuncion opens at the same 03:00Z). The test comment at :242-246 says exactly this. Whether the helper should land post-gap (Temporal `compatible`) is a datetime.ts question outside #30076 and I do not carry it as a finding; it costs a 1-hour sliver before the day at every midnight gap for every preset, and both bounds of this PR's windows are rendered through that one helper, so they stay consistent with the 13.
5. Should-fix 2 (stale prose): closed. packages/verify/README.md:44 "under each preset", :168-169 "never after today, except a forward preset's own edges, which are future days"; content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx:2595 the same clause, :2600 "under each preset"; ui/packages/plugin-dashboard/README.md:415 lists `next_month | next_quarter | next_30_days | custom`. A head-wide grep for "13 presets"/"each of the 13"/"thirteen" finds only CHANGELOGs, releases and an unrelated FeedItemType sentence; nothing in packages/**, ui/** or hand-written docs. cli.mdx:2595 is one long line; a wrapping nit only, and the body says the docs gates ran green on it.
6. Should-fix 3 (body): closed in r1 with one leftover. The objectql line now reads "does not iterate the list: it judges a comparand by the field's declared type", matching temporal-comparand-door.ts as reviewed. Follow-ups section names #30134 (p3, `next_week_end`/`next_year_end`) and #30140 (p2, compareTo), both open and routed `domain:ui`; #30140 carries Blocked-by #30076. The Server bullet describes the noon anchor and the Asuncion measurement; the DST table has the two rows; the Docs bullet names the three prose files; counts are consistent (71 + 2 = 73 in analytics-date-range.test.ts). Leftover: the Server bullet's second sentence still says "with the reference instant at the start of that day in the same zone" and then contradicts itself two sentences later ("stands at noon of the anchor day, not its first instant").
